sentence: This project discusses how membrane proteins, including channels, transporters and receptors, are built and how they work among membrane lipids and proteins.
This project tries to find out which molecules keep human keloid scars growing, using mathematical modeling, gene expression tests and human skin transplanted onto mice.
This project tests whether an antibiotic that is not absorbed can reduce inflammation and fibrosis in newborn piglets with a tied bile duct.
This project uses wearable sensors to measure how infants and young boys with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy move.
This project studies how cell cycle proteins in T cells affect their ability to enter and survive in solid tumors.
This project builds a tool that uses portable imaging and machine learning to find and predict oral diseases remotely.
This project tries to find out which biological processes link breathing to generalized seizures in epilepsy.
This project studies how noise damages sensory hair cells and causes hearing loss, using mice exposed to different levels of noise.
This project builds an app that helps therapists set up talking tappable grids of words for autistic children during play.
This project tests small molecules that reduce the clumping of hyperphosphorylated tau in Alzheimer's disease, using a rodent model.
This project tries to find out how the opioid enkephalin controls inflammation and the sensations of itch and pain in the skin.
This project uses machine learning and large sets of structure and function data to predict how T cell receptors recognize tumor antigens.
This project tries to find out how neurotensin guides valence processing and compulsive cocaine seeking in the basolateral amygdala.
This project studies how glioblastoma cells change to survive treatment and whether targeting the epigenetic processes behind this change can stop tumor recurrence.
This project builds computer methods that predict how a person's genetic variants change the way genes are controlled.
This project studies the cells and molecules inside human tuberculosis granulomas to learn how they fight the bacterium that causes tuberculosis and add to disease.
This project studies whether poor sleep contributes to Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, using data from many community-based cohort studies.
This project tests whether an antioxidant taken by mouth protects mouse models of age-related macular degeneration, a disease that can cause loss of central vision.
This project uses animal models and imaging to study how faulty organelle-specific autophagy leads to brain injury after blood flow returns.
This project builds a compact endoscope with a low-voltage electrowetting element to take detailed forward-viewing images of the heart.
